explanation: Connes (arXiv:2602.04022, §4.1): with W_p(f) = log p Σ_{m≥1} p^{-m/2}(f(p^m) + f(p^{-m})) and W_ℝ(f) = (log 4π + γ) f(1) + ∫_1^∞ (f(x) + f(x^{-1}) − 2x^{-1/2} f(1)) x^{1/2}/(x − x^{-1}) d*x, RH ⇔ Σ_v W_v(g ⋆ g*) ≤ 0 for all g ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ*₊) with ĝ(±i/2) = 0, where g*(x) = conj g(x^{-1}). Under x = e^u these become exactly weilNonArchimedean and weilArchimedean, g* becomes g(−u), ĝ(±i/2) = 0 becomes ∫ g e^{±u/2} = 0 (IsTestFunction), and multiplicative convolution becomes additive convolution. Restricting to real-valued g suffices: both W_v are invariant under x ↦ x^{-1}, so for g = a + ib the cross terms cancel, Q(g) = Q(a) + Q(b), and the vanishing conditions split. Faithful.
